Two Workers Rescued After Nepal Floods Swamp Hydropower Tunnel

A glacial collapse near Nepal's border with China triggered unprecedented flash floods that inundated hydropower projects, including the Trishul 3A tunnel. Nepali authorities have rescued 279 people from affected hydropower sites. Two tunnel workers were rescued alive from a depth of 170 metres nine days after the flood. Nepal has demanded compensation from India, the United States and China, describing it as a legal and moral liability issue. Scientific analysis points to bedrock as a likely factor in the flash floods. International aid includes an additional S$170,000 from the Singapore Red Cross, raising total contributions to over S$3 million, while agencies warn of a possible secondary crisis from water shortages and sanitation problems. The Nepal Army assisted survivors in Nuwakot district to cross a river.
